sentences.text: A horse can sleep standing up.
It does not fall over.
Its legs do not get tired.
This sounds impossible.
Stand up and close your eyes.
You will move a little.
Your muscles are working all the time.
A horse has a different system.
In its legs there are cords.
They can lock the joints in place.
Like a small hook, inside the leg.
The horse switches the hook on.
Then the leg holds itself.
No muscle is needed.
It can stand like this for hours.
Why would an animal need this?
Because a horse is food for something.
sentences.translationRu: Потому что лошадь для кого-то еда.

sentences.text: On open grass there is nowhere to hide.
The only answer is running away.
Getting up takes time.
Several seconds, which is too many.
Standing means running immediately.
But there is a problem with this.
Standing sleep is light sleep.
Deep sleep needs the body to go soft.
sentences.translationRu: Для глубокого сна тело должно расслабиться.

sentences.text: And a soft horse falls down.
So horses must lie down sometimes.
For about thirty minutes a day.
Usually in short pieces.
Without it they become ill.
In a group, they take turns.
sentences.translationRu: В табуне они делают это по очереди.

sentences.text: Some lie down. Others stand and watch.
sentences.translationRu: Одни ложатся. Другие стоят и смотрят.

sentences.text: Then they change.
Cows do something similar.
So do some birds, on one leg.
sentences.translationRu: И некоторые птицы, на одной ноге.

sentences.text: Sleeping is dangerous for a lot of animals.
Each one has found a way around it.

title: Why a boxing ring is square

sentences.text: Boxers fight in a square.
Four ropes. Four corners.
But everybody calls it a ring.
A ring is a circle.
So why the wrong word?
Because it used to be true.
sentences.translationRu: Потому что когда-то оно было верным.

sentences.text: Old fights had no building.
sentences.translationRu: У старых боёв не было здания.

sentences.text: They happened in a field or a street.
sentences.translationRu: Они проходили в поле или на улице.

sentences.text: People stood around to watch.
A crowd standing around makes a circle.
That circle was the ring.
Sometimes they drew it on the ground.
Fighters had to stay inside the line.
sentences.translationRu: Бойцы должны были оставаться внутри линии.

sentences.text: There were problems with this.
The crowd moved.
People pushed a fighter back in.
Or held him for the other man.
Friends of one boxer stood together.
So one side of the circle was not safe.
sentences.translationRu: И одна сторона круга становилась опасной.

sentences.text: In 1838 new rules arrived.
The fight would be in a square.
sentences.translationRu: Бой должен был идти в квадрате.

sentences.text: With ropes and posts at the corners.
sentences.translationRu: С канатами и столбами по углам.

sentences.text: About seven metres on each side.
The crowd was now outside the ropes.
Ropes are easy to build.
Four posts and four straight lines.
A circle of rope would sag.
And be hard to make the same twice.
sentences.translationRu: И повторить его дважды было бы трудно.

sentences.text: A square is also better for judging.
Corners give a fighter nowhere to go.
Which is part of the sport now.
Being pushed into a corner is a real thing.
sentences.translationRu: Быть загнанным в угол — реальная вещь.

sentences.text: In a circle there are no corners.
The fight would be different.
So the name stayed and the shape changed.
sentences.translationRu: Так что имя осталось, а форма изменилась.

sentences.text: Which happens with a lot of words.

title: Why the sun turns red in the evening

sentences.text: At midday the sun is white or yellow.
sentences.translationRu: В полдень солнце белое или жёлтое.

sentences.text: In the evening it is orange, then red.
Nothing about the sun has changed.
sentences.translationRu: С самим солнцем ничего не произошло.

sentences.text: What changed is the air.
Or rather, how much of it.
Sunlight is made of many colours.
sentences.translationRu: Солнечный свет состоит из многих цветов.

sentences.text: Air is full of very small pieces of gas.
sentences.translationRu: Воздух полон очень мелких частиц газа.

sentences.text: Light hits them and bounces away.
sentences.translationRu: Свет ударяется в них и отскакивает.

sentences.text: But not all colours bounce the same.
sentences.translationRu: Но не все цвета отскакивают одинаково.

sentences.text: Blue light bounces much more than red.
Blue is a short wave.
Small pieces of gas catch short waves.
Long waves mostly pass by.
sentences.translationRu: Длинные волны в основном проходят мимо.

sentences.text: So the blue is thrown around the sky.
sentences.translationRu: Поэтому синий разбрасывает по всему небу.

sentences.text: Which is why the sky is blue.
You are seeing light that has bounced.
At midday the sun is high.
Its light comes almost straight down.
sentences.translationRu: Его свет идёт почти прямо вниз.

sentences.text: A short path through the air.
Only some blue is taken out.
So the sun looks nearly white.
In the evening it is low.
Now the light comes in at an angle.
It travels much further through the air.
sentences.translationRu: И проходит через воздух гораздо дальше.

sentences.text: Many times further.
So almost all the blue is bounced away.
Then the green goes too.
What is left is orange and red.
That is the whole explanation.
Dust and smoke make it stronger.
More pieces means more bouncing.
This is why sunsets are famous
after a big fire or a volcano.
Clean air gives a quieter sunset.
sentences.translationRu: Чистый воздух даёт более скромный закат.

sentences.text: Astronauts see no sunset colours in space.
sentences.translationRu: В космосе астронавты цветов заката не видят.

sentences.text: No air, no bouncing, no red.
sentences.translationRu: Нет воздуха — нет рассеяния — нет красного.

sentences.text: The sun is simply white, and then gone.
sentences.translationRu: Солнце просто белое, а потом его нет.

sentences.text: Wash your hands with water alone.
The oil stays.
Add soap and it goes.
Soap is not killing the dirt.
Mostly it is not killing anything.
sentences.translationRu: В основном оно вообще ничего не убивает.

sentences.text: It is carrying things away.
Water and oil do not mix.
Everybody knows this from a kitchen.
Water likes water. Oil likes oil.
sentences.translationRu: Вода любит воду. Жир любит жир.

sentences.text: Neither wants the other.
Dirt on your hands is mostly oily.
sentences.translationRu: Грязь на руках в основном жирная.

sentences.text: So water runs past it and leaves it there.
sentences.translationRu: Поэтому вода проходит мимо и оставляет её.

sentences.text: A soap molecule is strange.
It has two ends, and they disagree.
sentences.translationRu: У неё два конца, и они не согласны.

sentences.text: One end loves water.
The other end hates water and loves oil.
sentences.translationRu: Другой воду не любит, а любит жир.

sentences.text: It is one thing, pulled two ways.
sentences.translationRu: Одна молекула, тянущаяся в две стороны.

sentences.text: Put soap in water on a dirty hand.
sentences.translationRu: Нанеси мыло с водой на грязную руку.

sentences.text: The oil-loving ends dig into the dirt.
sentences.translationRu: Концы, любящие жир, врезаются в грязь.

sentences.text: The water-loving ends point outwards.
They surround a drop of oil.
Like many small hands holding it.
sentences.translationRu: Как множество маленьких рук, держащих её.

sentences.text: Now the outside of that ball loves water.
sentences.translationRu: Теперь снаружи этот шарик любит воду.

sentences.text: So water can carry the whole thing away.
sentences.translationRu: И вода может унести его целиком.

sentences.text: The oil never mixed with the water.
sentences.translationRu: Жир с водой так и не смешался.

sentences.text: It was wrapped in something that did.
sentences.translationRu: Его завернули в то, что смешалось.

sentences.text: This also explains scrubbing.
Rubbing breaks the oil into small drops.
sentences.translationRu: Трение разбивает жир на мелкие капли.

sentences.text: Small drops are easier to surround.
And it explains the twenty seconds.
Surrounding takes time.
Two seconds of soap does almost nothing.
sentences.translationRu: Две секунды с мылом почти ничего не дают.

sentences.text: With some germs, soap does more.
sentences.translationRu: С некоторыми микробами мыло делает больше.

sentences.text: Certain viruses have an oily coat.
Soap pulls that coat apart.
The virus falls to pieces.
So soap does two jobs at once.
sentences.translationRu: Так что мыло делает две работы сразу.

sentences.text: It carries dirt away.
And it takes some things apart on the way.
sentences.translationRu: И по дороге кое-что разбирает на части.

sentences.text: Many animals produce tears.
Eyes need to stay wet.
And they need to wash things out.
Cut an onion and any mammal's eyes water.
sentences.translationRu: Разрежь лук — и у любого млекопитающего заслезятся глаза.

sentences.text: What appears to be human
is crying because of how you feel.
No other animal is known to do it.
sentences.translationRu: Ни за одним другим животным это не замечено.

sentences.text: Which is strange, if you think about it.
Emotion is not rare among animals.
Grief, fear and distress are widespread.
But water from the eyes is ours.
The tears themselves are different too.
Emotional tears carry more protein.
Which makes them thicker.
So they run more slowly down a face.
And stay visible for longer.
That detail points at the likely explanation.
sentences.translationRu: Эта деталь указывает на вероятное объяснение.

sentences.text: The leading account is that crying is a signal.
A visible one, addressed to other people.
It says something a face alone cannot.
sentences.translationRu: Он говорит то, чего одно лицо сказать не может.

sentences.text: I need help, and I am not a threat.
sentences.translationRu: Мне нужна помощь, и я не угроза.

sentences.text: Tears blur the crier's own vision.
Which is a genuine cost.
An animal that cannot see clearly
is announcing that it is not about to fight.
A signal that costs something is believable.
sentences.translationRu: Сигнал, который чего-то стоит, вызывает доверие.

sentences.text: This fits what the effect is on other people.
sentences.translationRu: Это сходится с тем, как он действует на других.

sentences.text: Photographs of faces with tears removed
sentences.translationRu: Фотографии лиц, с которых убрали слёзы,

sentences.text: are read as sadder but less specific.
sentences.translationRu: читаются как грустные, но менее определённые.

sentences.text: Add the tears and observers report
a clear urge to help.
The second account is about the body.
Crying usually happens as distress falls.
sentences.translationRu: Плач обычно начинается, когда напряжение спадает.

sentences.text: Not at the worst moment, but after it.
sentences.translationRu: Не в худший момент, а после него.

sentences.text: Which is why people cry at good news too.
sentences.translationRu: Поэтому плачут и от хороших новостей.

sentences.text: And after danger has already passed.
The two accounts do not compete.
sentences.translationRu: Эти версии не спорят друг с другом.

sentences.text: One is about what it does to you.
sentences.translationRu: Одна про то, что это делает с тобой.

sentences.text: The other about what it does to the room.
sentences.translationRu: Другая — про то, что это делает с комнатой.

title: Your phone would be wrong by ten kilometres a day

sentences.text: A phone finds itself using satellites.
Around thirty of them, high above.
sentences.translationRu: Их около тридцати, высоко над нами.

sentences.text: Each carries an extremely accurate clock.
And each broadcasts one message, continuously.
sentences.translationRu: И каждый непрерывно передаёт одно сообщение.

sentences.text: This is my position, and this is the time.
sentences.translationRu: Вот моя позиция, и вот время.

sentences.text: Your phone does not measure distance.
It measures delay.
The signal left at a known moment.
It arrived a fraction later.
Multiply by the speed of light
and you have the distance to that satellite.
Do that with four of them
and only one point in space fits.
sentences.translationRu: и подойдёт лишь одна точка в пространстве.

sentences.text: So the whole system is a clock problem.
sentences.translationRu: Значит, вся система — задача о часах.

sentences.text: An error of one millionth of a second
is an error of three hundred metres.
Which is where it becomes interesting.
A clock on a satellite does not run
at the same rate as a clock on the ground.
sentences.translationRu: не с той же скоростью, что часы на земле.

sentences.text: Two separate effects, pulling opposite ways.
sentences.translationRu: Два разных эффекта, тянущих в разные стороны.

sentences.text: The satellite is moving very fast.
A moving clock runs slow.
That costs about seven millionths of a second a day.
sentences.translationRu: Это стоит примерно семь миллионных секунды в сутки.

sentences.text: The satellite is also far from the Earth.
Gravity is weaker up there.
A clock in weaker gravity runs fast.
sentences.translationRu: В более слабой гравитации часы идут быстрее.

sentences.text: That gains about forty-five millionths a day.
sentences.translationRu: Это даёт примерно сорок пять миллионных в сутки.

sentences.text: The two do not cancel.
The net result is around thirty-eight.
Which sounds like nothing
until you multiply it by the speed of light.
sentences.translationRu: пока не умножишь на скорость света.

sentences.text: Ten kilometres of error, every day,
accumulating.
So the clocks are built deliberately wrong.
They are set to tick at the wrong rate
before launch, so that in orbit
they tick correctly for us.
Which makes satellite navigation
the most widely used demonstration
of a theory most people think is abstract.
Every phone in a pocket
is correcting for the shape of time.

title: The animal that survived being thrown into space

sentences.text: A tardigrade is about half a millimetre long.
It lives in moss, in soil, in gutters.
sentences.translationRu: Она живёт во мху, в почве, в водостоках.

sentences.text: It has eight legs and walks slowly.
sentences.translationRu: У неё восемь ног, и ходит она медленно.

sentences.text: It is not rare. It is almost everywhere.
sentences.translationRu: Она не редкость. Она почти везде.

sentences.text: There is probably one within a metre of you
sentences.translationRu: Вероятно, одна есть в метре от тебя,

sentences.text: if you are anywhere near a plant.
sentences.translationRu: если рядом есть хоть какое-то растение.

sentences.text: What it is famous for is not dying.
sentences.translationRu: Знаменита она тем, что не умирает.

sentences.text: In 2007 a number of them were taken to orbit
sentences.translationRu: В 2007 году некоторое их число вывели на орбиту

sentences.text: and put outside the spacecraft.
Vacuum. Cosmic radiation. Unfiltered sunlight.
sentences.translationRu: Вакуум. Космическое излучение. Нефильтрованный солнечный свет.

sentences.text: Many of them came back and reproduced.
The mechanism is not toughness.
A tardigrade is not armoured.
Step on one and it dies like anything else.
sentences.translationRu: Наступи на неё — умрёт, как и всё остальное.

sentences.text: What it can do is stop.
When conditions become impossible
it pulls in its legs and expels its water.
sentences.translationRu: она втягивает ноги и вытесняет воду.

sentences.text: Almost all of it, down to a few per cent.
It becomes a dry barrel.
Metabolism stops, or nearly stops.
It is not asleep. It is not hibernating.
sentences.translationRu: Это не сон. Это не спячка.

sentences.text: It is, by most definitions, not alive.
sentences.translationRu: По большинству определений она не жива.

sentences.text: And it can restart, years later, in water.
sentences.translationRu: И может запуститься снова, годы спустя, в воде.

sentences.text: Water is the problem being solved.
Almost everything that kills a cell
works through water.
Ice crystals tear membranes.
Radiation mostly damages by splitting water
sentences.translationRu: Радиация повреждает в основном расщепляя воду

sentences.text: into fragments that attack everything nearby.
sentences.translationRu: на обломки, которые бьют по всему вокруг.

sentences.text: Remove the water and most of that stops.
sentences.translationRu: Убери воду — и большая часть этого прекращается.

sentences.text: The trick is surviving the drying itself.
sentences.translationRu: Фокус в том, чтобы пережить само высыхание.

sentences.text: Which normally destroys a cell as thoroughly.
sentences.translationRu: А оно обычно губит клетку не менее надёжно.

sentences.text: They fill themselves with special proteins
that set into a glass as the water leaves.
sentences.translationRu: которые застывают в стекло по мере ухода воды.

sentences.text: Everything delicate is held in place
by a solid that is not a crystal.
Research now tries to borrow this.
Vaccines that need refrigeration
are expensive and fail in hot countries.
sentences.translationRu: дороги и подводят в жарких странах.

sentences.text: Dried in the same glass, some survive
sentences.translationRu: Высушенные в том же стекле, некоторые выживают

sentences.text: at room temperature for months.
Which would be a considerable thing
sentences.translationRu: А это было бы немалым делом,

sentences.text: to have learned from something in a gutter.
sentences.translationRu: если научиться этому у чего-то из водостока.

title: A quarter of the northern hemisphere is frozen ground

sentences.text: Permafrost is ground that has stayed frozen
sentences.translationRu: Вечная мерзлота — это грунт, остававшийся мёрзлым

sentences.text: for at least two consecutive years.
Most of it has been frozen far longer.
Tens of thousands of years in places.
It underlies roughly a quarter
of the land in the northern hemisphere.
It is not simply cold soil.
It is a store, and what it stores
is everything that failed to rot.
In a temperate forest, a fallen leaf
is consumed within a year or two.
The carbon in it returns to the air.
sentences.translationRu: Углерод из него возвращается в воздух.

sentences.text: In the far north, decomposition nearly stops.
sentences.translationRu: На дальнем севере разложение почти останавливается.

sentences.text: Plant matter accumulates instead
and then freezes, unfinished.
This has been happening since the last ice age.
The quantity involved is the point.
Estimates put the carbon in permafrost
at roughly twice what is in the atmosphere.
sentences.translationRu: примерно вдвое выше того, что в атмосфере.

sentences.text: It has simply been out of circulation.
sentences.translationRu: Он просто был выведен из оборота.

sentences.text: Held still by temperature.
Warming restarts the process
that was paused rather than finished.
sentences.translationRu: который был поставлен на паузу, а не завершён.

sentences.text: Microbes resume work they had begun
before the last ice age.
And they release what they produce.
Which gas depends on the water.
sentences.translationRu: Какой именно газ — зависит от воды.

sentences.text: Dry ground produces carbon dioxide.
Waterlogged ground produces methane,
which traps far more heat per molecule.
sentences.translationRu: который на молекулу удерживает куда больше тепла.

sentences.text: And thawing ground frequently becomes waterlogged,
sentences.translationRu: А оттаивающий грунт часто становится переувлажнённым,

sentences.text: because the ice that was holding its shape
sentences.translationRu: потому что лёд, державший его форму,

sentences.text: is the thing that has melted.
The surface then collapses.
Which produces the second problem.
Roads, pipelines, runways and buildings
sentences.translationRu: Дороги, трубопроводы, взлётные полосы и здания

sentences.text: across the north were built on the assumption
that the ground was permanent.
It was, for as long as anyone measured.
sentences.translationRu: Он и был — ровно столько, сколько его измеряли.

sentences.text: The engineering difficulty is unusual.
A foundation can be built for soft ground
sentences.translationRu: Фундамент можно строить под мягкий грунт

sentences.text: or for hard ground.
Building for ground that changes category
sentences.translationRu: Строить под грунт, который меняет категорию

sentences.text: part way through a structure's life
is a different problem entirely.

title: A translator writes the book a second time

sentences.text: A translated novel carries two names now.
sentences.translationRu: На переводном романе теперь два имени.

sentences.text: That change is recent and was argued for.
sentences.translationRu: Перемена недавняя, и за неё пришлось побороться.

sentences.text: For most of publishing history
the translator appeared in small print, or not at all.
sentences.translationRu: переводчик появлялся мелким шрифтом или никак.

sentences.text: The assumption behind that is worth naming.
sentences.translationRu: Стоящее за этим допущение стоит назвать.

sentences.text: It treats translation as transport.
The book exists; somebody moves it.
Nothing is added, so nobody is owed a name.
sentences.translationRu: Ничего не добавлено — значит, имени никто не должен.

sentences.text: Anybody who has compared two translations
of the same novel knows this is false.
sentences.translationRu: одного романа, знает, что это неправда.

sentences.text: They are recognisably different books.
Different rhythms, different jokes,
different characters, occasionally.
The reason is that almost nothing
sentences.translationRu: Причина в том, что почти ничто

sentences.text: maps cleanly from one language to another.
sentences.translationRu: не переносится чисто из языка в язык.

sentences.text: Take the simplest case, a pun.
A pun depends on two meanings
sharing one sound in one language.
sentences.translationRu: делящих один звук в одном языке.

sentences.text: There is no procedure for moving it.
A translator must invent a new joke
that does the same work in the same place
sentences.translationRu: которая делает ту же работу на том же месте

sentences.text: out of entirely different material.
Which is writing, not transport.
sentences.translationRu: А это письмо, а не перевозка.

sentences.text: Register is harder and less visible.
Languages divide formality differently.
Two characters who move from polite address
sentences.translationRu: Два персонажа, переходящие с вежливого обращения

sentences.text: to familiar address in one sentence
have just changed their entire relationship.
sentences.translationRu: только что изменили все свои отношения.

sentences.text: English cannot do that at all.
A translator has to rebuild the moment
out of word choice and rhythm
and hope the reader feels the shift.
sentences.translationRu: и надеяться, что читатель почувствует сдвиг.

sentences.text: Then there is the question with no answer.
How foreign should a translation feel?
Smooth it into the target language
and something specific is quietly deleted.
Leave the strangeness in
and readers call the prose clumsy.
Both choices are defensible.
Neither is invisible.
Which is the argument for the second name.
sentences.translationRu: В этом и довод за второе имя.

sentences.text: Not fairness, though that as well.
sentences.translationRu: Не справедливость, хотя и она тоже.

sentences.text: Accuracy. Somebody made those decisions,
and the reader is entitled to know who.
